steps.prompt: You can make one video. How do you ship fifty — safely?
steps.sub: Scale isn't just speed. It's using assets that won't get you a takedown, batching the work, and serving more than one language. By the end you'll know how to publish without a copyright strike — and at volume.

steps.prompt: What does "copyright-clean" actually mean for your video?

options.t: It went viral, so nobody will complain.
Every asset — music, footage, voice, visuals — is license-safe, so the whole video is safe to monetize.
You credited the original creators in the description.

steps.why: Credit in the description doesn't grant a license, and going viral just makes a claim more likely. Copyright-clean means every ingredient is something you're actually allowed to use commercially — license-safe music, models, and footage — so the finished video can be monetized without a takedown.
hints: A credit line isn't permission. What is?
If even one asset isn't license-safe, the whole video is exposed.

steps.prompt: The four levers of publishing at scale.
steps.sub: Tap each card. Together they turn one video into many.

cards.b: Use license-safe music + AI models + footage so every video is safe to monetize.
Run the same pipeline over many scripts at once, instead of one video start-to-finish.
Re-narrate + re-caption over the SAME visuals to ship another language cheaply.
Get the finished MP4 onto your channel — title, thumbnail, schedule, upload.

steps.prompt: Sort each asset: safe to use, or a strike waiting to happen?
steps.sub: Tap an asset, then the bin.

items.t: Music generated by a license-clean model you're allowed to monetize
A chart-topping pop song ripped from the radio
AI-generated visuals from a model whose license permits commercial use
A movie clip you grabbed because you credited the studio

hints: Ask of each: am I actually licensed to use this for money?
A credit line is not a license. Ripped songs and movie clips are claims waiting to happen.

steps.prompt: Order the steps to localize one finished video into a second language.
steps.sub: Tap them first to last. The whole point is to reuse, not rebuild.
chips: Translate the script into the target language
Re-narrate the new script with TTS in that language
Re-caption with the new word timings
Keep the same visuals + music bed
Re-composite and render the localized MP4
hints: The savings come from reusing visuals and music — lock those in first.
Then it's translate → re-voice → re-caption → re-render. Same backbone, new audio + text.

steps.prompt: Take a winning video global, the cheap way.
steps.sub: Your English short did well. Pick the next move to ship a Hindi version at low cost.
steps.goal: Localize one video without rebuilding it from scratch.

turns.situation: You have a finished English MP4 with visuals, music, voice, and captions. You want a Hindi version.
options: Reshoot everything from scratch in Hindi
Reuse the existing visuals + music, change only what's language-specific
Just auto-translate the title and call it done

turns.situation: Visuals and music are locked. The English voice and captions don't fit Hindi viewers.
options: Translate the script, then re-narrate it with a Hindi TTS voice
Keep the English narration but add a Hindi title

turns.situation: New Hindi narration exists. The on-screen captions are still in English and out of sync.
options: Re-caption with the new Hindi word timings
Leave English captions over Hindi audio
turns.log: 🔤 Re-caption → Hindi, synced to new audio

turns.situation: Two languages, same visuals. Now you want to do this across 12 scripts, not just one.
turns.q: How do you make this scale?
options: Batch the pipeline over all 12 scripts at once
Hand-edit each of the 12 one at a time forever
Only ever publish one video a month

hints: Localization = reuse visuals + music, swap voice + captions.
Scale = run the same pipeline over many scripts at once, not one by one.

steps.sub: Tap True or False for each, then check all at once.

statements.t: Crediting a song's artist in the description makes it safe to monetize.
statements.why: False — credit is not a license. To monetize safely you need assets you're actually permitted to use commercially, like license-clean generated music.

statements.t: Localizing usually means reusing the visuals and only swapping voice + captions.
statements.why: True — the expensive part (visuals) is reusable across languages. Re-narrate and re-caption over the same backbone and you've shipped another market cheaply.

statements.t: Batching means running the pipeline over many scripts instead of finishing one video at a time.
statements.why: True — that's exactly how you go from one video to fifty: feed many scripts through the same stages rather than babysitting each one end-to-end.

statements.t: Once it's rendered, the job's done — publishing is automatic.
statements.why: False — distribution is its own stage: title, thumbnail, schedule, and the actual upload to your channel. A great MP4 sitting on your drive earns nothing.

hints: Two of these confuse "credit" or "render" with the real requirement.
Reuse the costly assets; treat publishing as a real step, not a freebie.

steps.prompt: You want to publish 5 videos a week across 2 languages — and never get a strike. What's the single most important rule to lock in first?

options.t: Use the trendiest background music, even if it's licensed to someone else.
Make sure every asset is copyright-clean before you scale — scale multiplies risk too.
Publish as fast as possible and deal with claims later.

steps.why: Scale multiplies everything — including legal risk. One risky asset in your template means every one of the 10 weekly videos carries it. Locking in copyright-clean assets up front is what lets you batch and localize safely instead of mass-producing strikes.
hints: If a risky song is in your template, how many videos inherit the problem?
Speed without clean assets just scales the danger. Fix the source first.

steps.prompt: Make it yours — your publishing plan.
steps.sub: Not graded. We'll use this to shape a realistic cadence for your channel.

fields.label: How many videos a week is realistic for you, and on which platform?
fields.ph: e.g. 3 YouTube Shorts a week / 1 long video + 2 reels

fields.label: A second language worth localizing into for your audience?
fields.ph: e.g. Hindi, Spanish, none yet — English only

steps.prompt: Tap ALL the practices that let you publish safely AT SCALE.
steps.sub: A couple of these feel productive but get you flagged or stuck. Pick only the safe-scaling ones.
chips: Batching many scripts through one pipeline
A real distribution step (title, thumbnail, upload)
Ripping trending songs and crediting them
Hand-building every video one at a time
steps.why: Safe scale = copyright-clean assets, batching, localization by reuse, and treating distribution as its own step. Ripped-but-credited songs invite strikes; hand-building each video kills the throughput that scale needs.
hints: Recall the four levers: clean assets, batching, localization, distribution.
If a practice either risks a strike or can't be repeated fast, it doesn't belong at scale.
